title: Customer questionnaire & SIEM / audit evidence compact
content:
Purpose:
This compact is a short, customer-facing draft that answers common security questionnaire items about RBAC (v2), our audit log schema, SIEM export mechanisms, and evidence automation for assessments. Aim: provide clear answers for sales/CS to paste into customer questionnaires, and a checklist for engineering to produce evidence artifacts quickly.

Audience:
- Customer security reviewers (technical)
- Sales / Customer Success responding to questionnaires
- Internal reviewers (security/product owners)

Status & notes to reviewers:
- Draft — please mark any vendor-specific wording that requires legal sign-off.
- Known gaps: sample log extracts for on-prem Private deployments need final formatting; ETA for automated Splunk HEC connector TBD (owner: Liam).

1) Short answers for questionnaires (copy-ready)
Q: Describe your RBAC model and how roles are granted and revoked.
A: Redwood RBAC v2 uses role-based principals scoped to account and project. Roles are composed of granular permissions (read, write, execute) mapped to API routes and console actions. Role assignments are auditable and can be done via the Console, the Admin API, or programmatically through our Terraform provider. Changes to role bindings are recorded in the audit log within 2 seconds and can be exported to customer SIEMs. For Private deployments, role sync via SCIM is supported.

Q: How do you capture and store audit logs? Provide schema overview.
A: All audit events (API calls, console actions, auth events, system changes, model rollouts) are emitted as structured JSON with a canonical audit schema. Events are written to the central audit shard and persisted to an immutable log store. Customers can configure exports (S3, syslog, Splunk HEC, Elastic Ingest) and set retention. Logs include timestamps (ISO8601), actor (user/service-id), action, target resource, request metadata (IP, user-agent), outcome (success/failure), trace_id, and optional request/response hashes for repro.

2) Example audit event (canonical schema) — pasteable sample
{
  "timestamp": "2024-10-01T18:22:05Z",
  "event_type": "role.assignment",
  "actor": "admin:aisha.verma@redwood.ai",
  "actor_id": "usr_0a1b2c",
  "target": "project:acme-payments",
  "role": "read-only-inference",
  "request_id": "req_9f8e7d6c",
  "ip": "198.51.100.42",
  "outcome": "success",
  "trace_id": "trace-4f3b2a",
  "metadata": {
    "method": "console",
    "notes": "granted during onboarding"
  }
}

(Note: canonical events are emitted flattened in our JSON logs for SIEM export; nested metadata is expanded to metadata_* keys in exported records when 'flatten_export' is enabled.)

3) SIEM export options (customer-facing summary)
- Push to S3 (parquet or gzipped json): batch delivery, commonly used for long-term retention and compliance exports.
- Splunk HEC: near-real-time events via HEC token with TLS; supports indexing time and sourcetypes.
- Elastic / OpenSearch ingest: HTTP bulk API with backpressure and retry.
- Syslog (RFC5424) or remote-syslog: for on-prem collectors or network appliances.
- Kafka topic (dedicated stream) for high-volume integrations.

Each export supports configurable filters (event types, projects, actors) and optional field redaction. For Hosted customers, we offer managed delivery; Dedicated and Private customers can run connectors in their own network.

4) Evidence automation & playbook for common questionnaire asks
Goal: turn manual evidence responses into a 5-step automated workflow to reduce time-to-respond.
- Inputs: Questionnaire item key (e.g., "Provide latest role binding log for scope X"), time-range, tenant/project id.
- Actions:
  1) Map questionnaire key -> audit query (prebuilt templates live in repo: /security/query-templates).
  2) Execute query against audit index with time-range and project filter.
  3) Apply redaction rules (PII masking, IP fuzzing, user-hash) when copying out.
  4) Package artifacts: sample events + signed digest + export manifest.
  5) (Optional) Upload package to customer S3 pre-signed URL or send to reviewer via SecureShare link.
- Owners: Product Security (evidence templates), Observability (query infra), Solutions Eng (customer delivery).

5) Retention, immutability, and replay
- Default retention for Hosted: 365 days for high-fidelity audit events; aggregated indexes retained 7 years by request.
- Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable by contract.
- Immutability: audit store supports append-only retention windows and write-once buckets for compliance attestations.
- Replay: audit events include trace_id and request_id for deterministic replay into debugging and our evaluation harness.

6) Privacy & redaction policy
- We classify fields as: sensitive (PII), operational (IP, agent), and contextual (resource names). Exports apply redaction based on customer policy; default is to mask user emails to hashed ids for exported bundles unless explicit consent is granted.

7) Controls mapping (quick reference)
- SOC 2: Audit logging, RBAC, change management evidence available on request.
- ISO 27001: Logs and retention policies map to A.12 (operations) and A.9 (access control).
- GDPR: PII handling and redaction options available; support for Subject Access Request artifacts via audit lookup.

8) Common questionnaire snippets (utilities for CS)
- "We support structured, exportable audit logs containing actor, action, target, timestamp, outcome, and request identifiers; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via S3, Splunk HEC, Elastic, syslog, or Kafka."
- "RBAC v2 provides scoped roles, scoping to account and project, and supports SCIM and API-based provisioning; all changes are auditable and exportable."

9) Developer notes / TODOs (internal)
- Provide a sample flattened CSV export for "role.assignment" and attach to evidence templates (owner: Ethan).
- Finalize Splunk HEC docs (endpoint examples + recommended sourcetypes) and update Confluence page.
- Add Terraform example for role creation + audit query to /repo/examples.

Appendix A — quick audit field dictionary (export-ready names)
- event_ts (ISO8601)
- event_type
- actor_type (user|service|system)
- actor_id
- actor_email_hash
- actor_ip
- resource_type
- resource_id
- action
- role_name
- request_id
- trace_id
- outcome
- src_region
- export_batch_id

Appendix B — redaction example (how we deliver masked exports)
- Original: actor: "aisha.verma@redwood.ai", ip: "198.51.100.42"
- Exported: actor_email_hash: "sha256:3a7f...", actor_ip: "198.51.xxx.xxx"
